title: Quantization run governance: execution metadata, artifact TTL, audit controls and accuracy gating
creator: Sasha Patel
description: Define and ship the calibration run governance features in Redwood Console that ensure quantization profile runs (FP8/INT8) produce auditable artifacts, obey TTL/retention policies, and gate rollouts based on accuracy validation. This ticket covers run metadata schema, artifact lifecycle (store/expire/archive), permission model for artifacts and run access, automated accuracy checks (A/B vs baseline), and UX for operators to inspect, approve, or reject calibration outputs.
acceptance_criteria: Console can start a calibration run with configurable profile settings (fp8/int8, per-layer overrides) and surface a unique run id and metadata in the run list.
Artifacts (quant profiles, calibration traces, inputs/outputs, eval results) are persisted with configurable TTL and a clear lifecycle state (active/archived/deleted) visible in the UI.
RBAC policies control who can view runs, download artifacts, and perform approvals; roles include Calibration-Viewer, Calibration-Operator, Calibration-Approver, and Admin.
Automated accuracy validation executes after run completion using a defined eval set; pass/fail status is recorded with numeric metrics and linked diffs to baseline.
Audit trail captures user actions (create, edit, approve, delete, TTL change) with timestamps and links to GitHub PRs or confluence artifacts where applicable.
Retention/TTL enforcement job runs daily and moves artifacts to archive or deletion state according to policy; operations team can override for legal holds.
API endpoints exist for external automation to query run status, fetch artifacts, and trigger revalidation; documented in the API reference.
Security review and KMS integration completed for artifact encryption at rest and access control checks for private deployments.
End-to-end smoke test (see test_plan) passes in staging and is included in the release checklist for console-2025.03.

decisions: Use stable run-id format: RID-{YYYYMMDD}-{shorthash} to make artifacts easily traceable across storage backends.
Store all artifacts in S3-compatible object store with server-side encryption using customer-managed KMS keys for Private deployments.
Retention policy defaults: 90 days for raw calibration traces, 365 days for quant profiles, indefinite for artifacts under legal hold.
Accuracy gate configurable threshold: default 99.5% of baseline for top-level metric, but project owners can set stricter bandings.
Approval flow requires a Calibration-Approver signoff for any profile released to Dedicated or Hosted production routes.
open_questions: Should archived artifacts be shallow-copied to cold storage (cheaper/longer) or kept in place behind stricter RBAC? Trade-offs between retrieval latency and cost.
How granular should the RBAC be for per-artifact permissions (e.g., allow download of quant profile but not raw traces)?
Do we expose TTL editing to Project Admins in the UI or require an API + ticket workflow for longer retention requests?
What is the audit retention policy for user actions themselves (we currently retain action logs for 2 years; security wants 5 years for enterprise customers).
test_plan: Create sample FP8 and INT8 calibration runs in staging with synthetic models and eval sets.
Verify run metadata surfaces correctly in list and detail UIs, and that run-id links resolve to artifact bundles.
Simulate TTL expiry: run daily TTL job in staging and confirm artifacts move to archive then deletion state as configured.
Exercise RBAC by validating access matrices for Calibration-Viewer, -Operator, and -Approver across hosted and private deployments.
Run accuracy gate tests against baseline and validate pass/fail propagation to release pipeline.
End-to-end smoke test for release: create run -> pass gate -> approve -> release profile to canary route.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable run metadata and artifact TTL features for 10% of orgs; monitor support tickets and storage behavior.
Phase 2 (beta): Add RBAC controls and approval flows for early enterprise customers with security review completed.
Phase 3 (general): Enable automated accuracy gates and archival policy; flip default TTL to production settings and publish docs.
Fallback: Admin API to roll back TTL enforcement and undelete artifacts within 72 hours when needed.
followups: PM to align with Legal on long-term audit retention (open question) and update defaults accordingly.
Design to produce an accessible artifact viewer for non-engineer stakeholders (QA/Compliance).
Engineering to add quota metrics for artifact storage to cost dashboard and alert on growth spikes.
Create run-export tooling for offline archiving and GDPR data subject requests.
